title: Median Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Median Calculator: Median (middle value) of a list of numbers. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to common questions.

The [Median Calculator](/median-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Median (middle value) of a list of numbers. Enter your numbers (separated by commas, spaces or new lines) and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Find the median of a list of numbers — the middle value when the numbers are sorted from smallest to largest. If there is an odd count, the median is the single middle number; if there is an even count, it is the average of the two middle numbers. The median is the go-to average when a few extreme values would drag the mean away from the typical value: house prices and incomes are usually reported as medians for exactly this reason.

## How to use the Median Calculator

Start by typing or pasting your numbers (separated by commas, spaces or new lines). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Paste or type your numbers, separated by commas, spaces or new lines.
2. Read the median — the sorted list is shown so you can check the middle.
3. Compare with the mean calculator when the list has extreme values.

## Formula

Sort the numbers. With an odd count n, the median is the value at position (n + 1) ÷ 2. With an even count, it is the average of the two middle values. For example, the median of 4, 8, 15, 16, 23 and 42 is (15 + 16) ÷ 2 = 15.5.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Median Calculator](/median-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. The median of 4, 8, 15, 16, 23 and 42 is 15.5: sorted, the two middle numbers are 15 and 16, and (15 + 16) ÷ 2 = 15.5. Try the same figures in the [Median Calculator](/median-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## Why house prices use the median

A street with nine £200,000 houses and one £5 million mansion has a mean price of £680,000, but the median is £200,000 — the price of a typical house on that street. The median ignores the mansion, which is why it is used for incomes, house prices and anything else where a few huge values would distort the picture.

## Median with an even count

With an even number of values there is no single middle number, so the median is defined as the average of the two middle values. This keeps the median consistent: adding one more value to the list moves the median smoothly instead of jumping between two neighbours.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- The sorted list is shown — count in from each end to find the middle.
- The median never has to be one of your numbers (with an even count it is an average).
- For skewed data, the median is usually more useful than the mean.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the median?

The middle value of a sorted list of numbers. Half the values are below it and half are above it. Try it with your own numbers in the [Median Calculator](/median-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How do you find the median with an even number of values?

Sort the numbers and average the two middle values. For 4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42 the middle pair is 15 and 16, so the median is 15.5. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.

### When should I use the median instead of the mean?

When the data has outliers — a few very large or very small values. The median is not pulled around by them, so it describes the typical value better. Try it with your own numbers in the [Median Calculator](/median-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is the median always one of the numbers in the list?

Only with an odd count. With an even count it is the average of the two middle numbers, which may not appear in the list. Try it with your own numbers in the [Median Calculator](/median-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.
